output.title: Design against untested assumptions by narrowing the decision
output.body:
The problem with automation is usually not the tool. It is the hidden assumption behind the workflow.

If you run a small business, the first question is not “Can AI do this?” It is “What exactly is the recurring decision I am trying to change?” That keeps the work bounded. A good candidate is a repetitive task already sitting in digital tools and English-language documents, with a measurable outcome and a clear human owner.

This is where untested assumptions show up. You may assume the data is clean, the approval path is simple, or the handover from manual work to a system will be obvious. In practice, those are separate questions. One demo is not proof that the live workflow will behave the same way.

So the next step is simple: write down one recurring workflow, how often it happens, what “done” means, and where human approval must stay in place. If the decision touches money movement or another high-risk action, the approval stays human.

That narrow view is less exciting than pretending the whole workflow is ready. It is also more useful.
